bureau: Credit Information System (Central Bank of Seychelles)
note: The Credit Reporting Act, 2023 (Act 20 of 2023), s. 29(3): negative data in the Central Bank's Credit Information System stays available to lenders five years from the borrower's full repayment, written as 1,826 days after payment; while unpaid it stays, written as thirty years, the longest the game keeps. Data providers submit at intervals the Central Bank specifies (s. 10(3)), so the days after a due date a missed payment is reported are the game's reading: the bureau's next monthly update.

sources.title: Credit Reporting Act, 2023 (Act 20 of 2023), Official Gazette of Seychelles, 20 November 2023 (Laws.Africa copy of the gazette)
sources.said: Negative data collected in the CIS shall be available to data users ... for a period of 5 years as from — ... the date of a data subject's full repayment of outstanding ... balances;

sources.title: Credit Reporting Act, 2023 (Act 20 of 2023), Official Gazette of Seychelles, 20 November 2023 (Laws.Africa copy of the gazette)
sources.said: A data provider shall submit information to the CIS at intervals ... specified by the Central Bank.
